titulo: Using the simple future to guess about the present
subtitulo: ¿Dónde estará? The future tense also says I wonder, probably and must be, about right now.
regla: To guess or speculate about what is probably true right now, use the simple future: ¿Dónde estará Beto? Estará en el agua.

bloques.texto: The **simple future** (**futuro simple**, also called **futuro imperfecto**) doesn't only talk about tomorrow. It also expresses **probability in the present**: what is probably happening at the moment you speak.
You're not saying what will happen, and you're not stating a fact. You are:

lista.texto: wondering what might be happening: **¿Dónde estará?** = _Where could he be? I wonder where he is._
saying what is probably happening: **Estará en el agua.** = _He's probably in the water._
guessing what must be going on: **Tendrá hambre.** = _He must be hungry._

bloques.texto: It works with any verb and with the future + gerund for actions in progress: **estará entrenando** = _he's probably training_. To guess the time, use **ser**: **serán las seis** = _it's probably about six_.

In everyday Mexican Spanish this is very common in questions to yourself: **¿Qué hora será?**, **¿Quién será?** when someone knocks at the door. You'll also hear **ha de** + infinitive with the same meaning: **ha de estar en el agua** = _he must be in the water_.
Tip: if you could add _I wonder_ or _probably_ in English, Spanish reaches for the future.

lista.en: Beto hasn't arrived yet. Where could he be?
He's not answering the phone; he's probably training.

lista.es: No traigo reloj, pero ==serán== como las seis.
lista.en: I don't have a watch, but it's probably about six.

lista.es: Hay muchos carros en la playa; ==habrá== buenas olas.
lista.en: There are lots of cars at the beach; there must be good waves.

lista.es: El cliente no encuentra la llave. ==La tendrá== en la otra chamarra.
lista.en: The customer can't find the key. He probably has it in his other jacket.

lista.es: No reconozco esta calle, pero ==estaremos== cerca de la taquería.
lista.en: I don't recognize this street, but we must be near the taquería.
Amos isn't saying anything. What could he be thinking?

bloques.texto: This future is about **now**, not about later. And if the guess is about the **past**, the future doesn't work: use the **conditional**. See [[5069|the conditional for guessing about the past]].

filas.t: Ayer Beto no vino; estará cansado.
Ayer Beto no vino; estaría cansado.

lista.nota: A guess about yesterday takes the conditional: **estaría** = _he was probably tired_.

filas.t: Hoy Beto no vino; estará cansado.

lista.nota: This one is right: a guess about now, so the future.

filas.t: No sé dónde está. Va a estar en el huerto.
No sé dónde está. Estará en el huerto.

lista.nota: **Ir a** is for plans and predictions about later, not for guessing what's happening now.

lista.texto: A prediction about the future: [[5162|the future for predictions]].
A plain future action: [[5155|regular verbs in the simple future]]. In speech, plans usually take [[7067|ir a]].
A guess about the past: [[5069|the conditional for probability in the past]].
A guess about something that has just happened: [[7266|the future perfect to talk about the past]].
The future + gerund for something in progress: [[9342|the progressive future]].
The future after a condition: [[6146|si + present, then the future]].

bloques.texto: Say it out loud, then open the answer.

lista.p: In Spanish: _I wonder what time it is._
lista.nota: A guess about now: **ser** in the future.

lista.p: Guess about now: Naomi no está en la cabina; ___ (estar) en la sala de máquinas.
lista.r: Naomi no está en la cabina; estará en la sala de máquinas.

lista.p: Which one, about last night? **Anoche no contestó; estará dormido** or **Anoche no contestó; estaría dormido**.
lista.nota: Guessing about the past takes the conditional.
